title: Crack Linear B Like Ventris
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: A p5.js five-step puzzle that replays a simplified version of the 1952 decipherment of Linear B: the sign count, Kober's triplet, the Cretan place-name guess, the grid that unlocks the other signs, and a test of the values on the Pylos tripod tablet (PY Ta 641), whose pictograms confirm the reading.

learningObjectives: Solve a simplified version of the 1952 decipherment by matching three Linear B sign groups to Cretan place names with grid clues and then using the resulting sound values to predict four objects on the Pylos tripod tablet, getting all three place names and at least 3 of 4 objects right on the first attempt.
prerequisites: Linear B and its spelling rules
Spelling Knossos the Mycenaean way (worked example)

dependencies: Noto Sans Linear B via Google Fonts

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Guided problem solving: two practice steps with retries, then two scored steps (first Check only) in which the learner applies the grid and tests the result against independent evidence
keyQuestions: What kind of script has about 90 sound-signs?
What do two signs share when only the ending of a word changes?
Which sign groups are Knossos, Amnisos, and Tylissos?
What objects do ti-ri-po-de, qe-to-ro-we, ti-ri-o-we-e, and a-no-we name?
commonMisconceptions: Decipherment starts by guessing the language.
Each Linear B sign is a letter, as in an alphabet.
A single lucky guess deciphered the script.
Linear B words look like Classical Greek words.
assessmentOpportunities: Step 3 first Check: three place names (mastery: 3 of 3).
Step 5 first Check: four tablet objects (mastery: at least 3 of 4).
Explain why the tripod tablet's pictograms convinced the doubters.
